title: Running at SoHo Playhouse in NYC until 8/2 #comedy #snl #musicaltheat...
transcript: SNL's Jane Wickline and comedian Liva Pierce take their comedic songwriting to the theater, turning the songs into a quirky two person musical called Dukes, in which they play comedically heightened versions of themselves as roommates running into absurd antics as they go about their day. The show *kinda* has a plot with some continuity; There's running gags like a search for a crystal goose, a deadly pizza restaurant, and an attractive neighbor that they both become entangled with. And throughout we get a sense of the distinct dynamic between these long time and somewhat codependent friends. But for the most part, the premise is kinda just a vehicle for the songs, which poke fun at everyday experiences by giving them absurd, often hilarious twists. The scenes are so blatantly reverse-engineered just to set up the next song that that kinda just becomes part of the joke. But even though they get away with that, the show is still a little rough around the edges. I'm not sure to what extent this is a work in progress, whether they plan to bring it back in a more polished form. I hope so, because I really enjoyed it and I do think it could use some tightening, both in terms of the run of show, which has a little too much dead air and awkward staging, but also distilling it down a bit. It seems like they're really trying to include as many of their songs as possible. And it ends Up being an 80 minute show with about 60 minutes’ worth of really good material. Having said all that, the show is still hilarious. Their sense of humor is extremely silly with an offbeat whimsy that definitely keeps us on our toes. And as much as the story is paper thin, it is genuinely a delight to follow the antics of this oddball duo.
classificationReason: First-hand review of Dukes at SoHo Playhouse with clear evaluative opinions: 'I really enjoyed it,' 'a little rough around the edges,' 'could use some tightening.' Creator clearly attended the production.
